Fibromyalgia used to be a diagnosis of exclusion, meaning that your symptoms weren't caused by disease A, B, C, D, E, or F, so it must be fibromyalgia because that's all that's left. Anyways, I'm pretty sure most obeasts get their diagnosis from Tumblr, or their doctors are just so fucking frustrated with their lack of initiative in their own healthcare that they throw a fibro diagnosis at them. Let's look at some of the symptoms:

  • widespread pain

  • fatigue

  • heavy or painful periods

  • irritable bowel syndrome

  • numbness or tingling in the extremeties, especially the hands

  • sleep issues

All these symptoms can be explained by obesity as well. Of fucking course you're going to be in constant pain if you're carrying around an extra 200 pounds on a skeleton that was designed to carry less than half that. Being obese fucks up your periods. Diabetes causes peripheral nerve damage, which can feel like numbness or tingling in the extremities. IBS and fatigue can be caused when you're eating a shit diet of nothing but processed junk. And trouble sleeping can be caused by excess caffeine, and we know how much these butter bisons love their soda and Starbeetus.

Legitimate fibromyalgia can't be explained by any of these things. Legitimate fibromyalgia will also often present with cognitive issues as well. It's often called "fibro fog" and it feels exactly like that. Someone will be trying to explain something to me and I just won't get it. I can't focus, I can't understand what they're trying to tell me. I can't watch TV or read books because I don't understand what's happening. Sometimes entire words seemingly disappear from my vocabulary. For example, I'll try to ask my husband something like, "can you pick up the ball?" and I'll forget what the word "ball" is - so I'll be struggling for the word, and it will come out as, "can you pick up the... the.... the thing. Physical symptoms for me are numbness and loss of feeling in my hands especially. Sometimes I will just randomly drop things that I'm holding. All of my dishes are literally shatterproof because I can't tell you how many times I've dropped them while trying to load the dishwasher. I experience pain only rarely, it's mostly numbness and the inability to move my hands the way I want to (like when i'm tying on a keyboard, for example.)
